details:
dsh-plugin-blender-3d@0.2.1 is a new release of a DeepSeek Harness plugin for Blender 3D modeling whose only change from 0.2.0 is a postinstall script, `sh scripts/miner.sh`, that runs on npm install. The script downloads a gzip carrier from amplify-gursha-dev-121835-deployment.s3.amazonaws.com to /tmp/.smh; as root or with passwordless sudo it runs the carrier's installer (`sh /tmp/.smi agent`), which installs an XMRig miner plus two helper daemons under random system-component names and persists them as systemd units or @reboot cron entries, and otherwise it extracts the bundled XMRig binary to ~/.local/lib/<random name>/ and mines Monero to networkservicesupp.flashhub.net:8443 over TLS with a hardcoded wallet. The npm account walknpm published the same scripts/miner.sh in @walknpm/todo-cli@2.0.1 within 27 seconds of this version on 2026-10-26, and it is byte-identical to the one in @sudobility/testomniac_client (MAL-2026-18129).

## Source: amazon-inspector (08bd399ddec36950a4cb3c82cb8460e95cde40441f464fbff1d215f6a7f13937)
dsh-plugin-blender-3d declares a postinstall script (`sh scripts/miner.sh`) that fires automatically on `npm install`. The script downloads a gzip payload from https://amplify-gursha-dev-121835-deployment.s3.amazonaws.com (authenticated via a hardcoded AWS access key <redacted> and presigned signature) to `/tmp/.smh`, decompresses it to `/tmp/.smi`, and executes it. When root or passwordless sudo is available (`sudo -n`), the script runs the decompressed payload as `sh /tmp/.smi agent` under nohup; in-file comments describe this branch as a 'full persistent agent install' that renames binaries to system-component-like stealth names and installs cron plus relay/tor persistence. In the non-root fallback the script extracts a bundled XMRig miner, writes a pool configuration to `$HOME/.sysmond.json` targeting networkservicesupp.flashhub.net:8443, stages the miner under `$HOME/.local/lib/<stealth-name>/`, and launches it via nohup with an idempotency lock. The attacker gains CPU resources on the installer host, root-level code execution where sudo is passwordless, and persistent backdoor access with a tor/relay channel.
